## A skill

Skills come from two sources. A pyskill is a Python module whose
docstring is the skill, published by an installed package (see
[pyskills](https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/pyskills)). A `SKILL.md` file
is a markdown file in a skills folder, in the Agent Skills layout. Both
become a
[`Skill`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/skills.html#skill), with
a name, a source, a description, and `where` it came from so a person
can go and read it.

A [`Skill`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/skills.html#skill)
holds a loader for its body, not the body, so finding skills does not
read every file. When no description is given, it is the body’s first
paragraph on one line.

`GROUP` is the entry-point group installed packages publish pyskills
under. `EXTRA_MODULES` lists modules that are skills but do not publish
one. `MAX_SKILL_CHARS` caps the length of a skill body sent to the
model.

``` python
GROUP, EXTRA_MODULES, MAX_SKILL_CHARS
```

    ('pyskills', ('exhash.skill',), 20000)

``` python
test_eq(GROUP, 'pyskills')
test_eq(EXTRA_MODULES, ('exhash.skill',))
test_eq(MAX_SKILL_CHARS, 20_000)
```

### describe

``` python
def describe(
    text, mx:int=300
):
```

*A one-line description from a skill body: its first paragraph,
collapsed.*

``` python
describe('''Search the web and read results into durable memory.

Use it when a question needs pages nobody has read yet.''')
```

    'Search the web and read results into durable memory.'

``` python
test_eq(describe(''), '')
test_eq(describe('one\ntwo\n\nthree'), 'one two')
test_eq(len(describe('x ' * 400)), 300)
```

`text()` loads the body when it is asked for and clips it to
`MAX_SKILL_CHARS`. A skill that cannot be read returns a message saying
so, instead of raising an exception into the agent’s turn.

``` python
s = Skill('nbdev', 'md', 'Develop nbdev projects.', 'nbs/SKILL.md', _text=lambda: 'the whole body')
def explodes(): raise FileNotFoundError('SKILL.md')
broken = Skill('gone', 'md', _text=explodes)
s.text(), broken.text()
```

    ('the whole body', 'could not read skill gone: FileNotFoundError: SKILL.md')

``` python
test_eq(s.text(), 'the whole body')
assert broken.text().startswith('could not read skill gone'), broken.text()
big = Skill('big', 'md', _text='x' * (MAX_SKILL_CHARS + 500))
test_eq(len(big.text()), MAX_SKILL_CHARS + len('\n…[500 more chars]'))
test_eq(s.dict()['where'], 'nbs/SKILL.md')
```

## Where skills come from

Installed packages publish pyskills under the `pyskills` entry-point
group. A module’s description comes from its docstring, and Python
offers no way to read a docstring without importing the module, so
discovery imports each pyskill module once. A module with an empty
docstring is skipped.

`SKILL.md` files are looked for in a list of folders, from lowest to
highest precedence, so that a later folder’s skill replaces an earlier
one with the same name.
[`skill_dirs`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/skills.html#skill_dirs)
returns the list. It starts with the `skills` folder inside `learned`,
for skills a tool wrote rather than a person, then the application’s
config folder `cfg`, then `~/.agents/skills` for a person’s own skills,
then `.leela/skills` and `.agents/skills` in each project root. A
project can therefore replace what a person set up for themselves, and a
skill a tool learned replaces an installed pyskill but loses to every
folder a person writes.

The `read_skill` tool reads the same installed skill that discovery
found through the `pyskills` entry point:

``` python
from shalya.host import LocalHost
from shalya.skills import discover
from shalya.tools import skill_tools
```

``` python
installed_skills = discover()
installed_host = LocalHost(index=False)
installed_read = {t.__name__: t for t in skill_tools(installed_host, lambda: installed_skills)}['read_skill']
installed_exhash = next(s for s in installed_skills if s.where == 'exhash.skill')
installed_body = installed_read(installed_exhash.name)
assert installed_body.startswith(f'<skill name="{installed_exhash.name}"')
assert len(installed_body) > 100 and 'exhash' in installed_body.lower()
```

A skills folder follows the Agent Skills layout: one folder per skill
holding a `SKILL.md`, whose optional frontmatter gives the name and
description. Without frontmatter the folder name is the skill’s name and
the first paragraph its description.

``` python
tmp = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
d = tmp/'.agents'/'skills'/'notebook-tests'
d.mkdir(parents=True)
(d/'SKILL.md').write_text('''---
name: notebook-tests
description: Write executable test cells in the notebook that owns the code.
---

Put the readable case in the notebook and the bulk assertions in `tests/`.
''')
plain = tmp/'.agents'/'skills'/'plain'
plain.mkdir()
(plain/'SKILL.md').write_text('Say what changed.\n\nAnd nothing else.\n')
[(s.name, s.description) for s in _md_skills(tmp/'.agents'/'skills')]
```

    [('notebook-tests',
      'Write executable test cells in the notebook that owns the code.'),
     ('plain', 'Say what changed.')]

``` python
got = {s.name: s for s in _md_skills(tmp/'.agents'/'skills')}
test_eq(sorted(got), ['notebook-tests', 'plain'])
test_eq(got['plain'].description, 'Say what changed.')     # no frontmatter: the first paragraph
assert 'bulk assertions' in got['notebook-tests'].text()
test_eq(got['notebook-tests'].source, 'md')
```

[`discover`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/skills.html#discover)
collects every source: pyskills, then the
[`skill_dirs`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/skills.html#skill_dirs)
folders, then the `extra` skills you pass. A later source replaces an
earlier skill of the same name, and the result is sorted by name.

[s.name for s in skills]

## The index

[`skill_index`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/skills.html#skill_index)
renders the block that goes into the system prompt: a heading, a line
telling the agent to call `read_skill(name)` before doing the work a
skill covers, and one line per skill with its name and description,
never its body. Each description is cut to `SKILL_DESC_MAX` characters
at a word boundary, so one long description cannot crowd out the rest.

[`find`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/skills.html#find) looks a
skill up by exact name, then by unique prefix, then by unique substring.
A name that matches several skills returns None instead of guessing, and
the `read_skill` tool then lists the skills that exist.

``` python
find(skills, 'notebook-tests').name, find(skills, 'notebook').name, find(skills, 'nope')
```

    ('notebook-tests', 'notebook-tests', None)

``` python
test_eq(find(skills, 'notebook-tests').name, 'notebook-tests')
test_eq(find(skills, 'notebook').name, 'notebook-tests')     # unique prefix
test_eq(find(skills, 'tests').name, 'notebook-tests')        # unique substring
test_eq(find(skills, 'nope'), None)
two = [Skill('edit', 'md'), Skill('editor', 'md')]
test_eq(find(two, 'edit').name, 'edit')                      # exact beats prefix
test_eq(find(two, 'edi'), None)                              # ambiguous prefix
```

## Extensions

An extension is a Python file a user drops in an extensions folder. It
defines `setup(reg)`, and through `reg`, a
[`Registry`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/skills.html#registry),
it may add tools, skills and slash commands, hook lifecycle events, and
replace the approval policy. That is all a
[`Registry`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/skills.html#registry)
offers: it gives an extension no access to the model, the engine or the
conversation history.

`EVENTS` lists the lifecycle events an extension may hook, such as
`before_tool` and `after_turn`. Hooking any other name raises an error,
so a typo cannot silently hook nothing.

``` python
EVENTS
```

    ('before_turn',
     'after_turn',
     'before_tool',
     'after_tool',
     'compact',
     'approval')

``` python
test_eq(EVENTS, ('session_start', 'before_turn', 'after_turn', 'before_tool', 'after_tool', 'stop', 'compact', 'approval', 'background_done', 'watch'))
test_eq(len(set(EVENTS)), len(EVENTS))
```

### shell_hooks

``` python
def shell_hooks(
    reg, path
):
```

*Register the hooks a `hooks.json` lists: `[{event, match, command}]`.*

`load(reg, roots, cfg)` runs every `.py` file in the extension folders
([`ext_dirs`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/skills.html#ext_dirs))
whose name does not start with `_`, plus any files or folders given in
`paths`, and calls its `setup(reg)`. It adds one line per file to
`reg.notes`: what the file registered, or why it failed to load. It also
registers the shell hooks listed in `<cfg>/hooks.json`
([`shell_hooks`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/skills.html#shell_hooks)).

A hook may return a value. `fire(event, ...)` runs the event’s hooks in
registration order and returns their return values, so a `before_tool`
hook can return a reason to deny the call or replacement arguments, and
an `after_tool` hook a rewritten result. A hook that raises is recorded
in `reg.notes` and skipped. A shell hook is a command listed in
`hooks.json` as `{event, match, command}`, where `match` is a glob on
the tool name. It receives the event as JSON on standard input and may
answer with a JSON object on standard output holding `deny`, `args` or
`result`. Anything else it prints is ignored.

A real extension, with a real `setup(reg)`, loaded from disk, alongside
a file that fails to load and one with no `setup`:

``` python
extdir = tmp/'extensions'
extdir.mkdir()
(extdir/'wc.py').write_text('''
def setup(reg):
    @reg.tool
    def word_count(path: str) -> str:
        "How many words are in a file."
        return str(len(open(path).read().split()))
    reg.command('wc', lambda agent, arg: 'counted ' + arg, help='count words')
    reg.skill('house-style', 'Dense lines. Short names.', 'How code is written here.')
''')
(extdir/'helpers.py').write_text('SHARED = 1\n')
(extdir/'boom.py').write_text('raise RuntimeError("no")\n')
reg = load(Registry(), cfg=tmp)
reg.notes
```

    ['boom.py: failed to load (RuntimeError: no)',
     'helpers.py: loaded, no setup()',
     'wc.py: 1 tool(s), 1 skill(s), 1 command(s)']

``` python
test_eq([t.__name__ for t in reg.tools], ['word_count'])
test_eq(list(reg.commands), ['wc'])
test_eq([s.name for s in reg.skills], ['house-style'])
test_eq(reg.skills[0].text(), 'Dense lines. Short names.')
test_eq(reg.tools[0](str(extdir/'helpers.py')), '3')          # the tool really runs
assert any('helpers.py: loaded, no setup()' in n for n in reg.notes), reg.notes
assert any(n.startswith('boom.py: failed to load') for n in reg.notes), reg.notes
```

``` python
(tmp/'hooks.json').write_text(json.dumps([
    {'event': 'before_tool', 'match': 'run_*',
     'command': "python3 -c 'import sys, json; d = json.load(sys.stdin); print(json.dumps({\"deny\": \"no rm\"}) if \"rm\" in d[\"args\"][2][\"command\"] else \"logged\")'"},
    {'event': 'nonsense', 'command': 'true'}]))
reg = load(Registry(), cfg=tmp)
test_eq(reg.fire('before_tool', None, 'run_shell', {'command': 'rm -rf x'}), ['no rm'])
test_eq(reg.fire('before_tool', None, 'run_shell', {'command': 'ls'}), [None])
test_eq(reg.fire('before_tool', None, 'view_file', {}), [None])
assert any(n.endswith('1 hook(s)') or 'skipped' in n for n in reg.notes), reg.notes
test_eq(reg.drop_loaded().hooks['before_tool'], [])
```

Reloading re-reads the extension files, and must not throw away what the
running program registered since.
[`load`](https://vedicreader.github.io/shalya/skills.html#load) records
which registrations came from the files (`mark` and `mark_loaded`), and
`drop_loaded` removes exactly those and keeps the rest. `loaded` says
whether the files are currently loaded.

``` python
live = load(Registry(), cfg=tmp)
def live_tool(x: str) -> str: return x
live.tool(live_tool); live.command('mine', lambda a, arg: arg); live.on('after_tool', print)
live.drop_loaded()
[t.__name__ for t in live.tools], list(live.commands), len(live.hooks['after_tool']), live.loaded
```

``` python
test_eq([t.__name__ for t in live.tools], ['live_tool'])   # the file's word_count went, mine stayed
test_eq(list(live.commands), ['mine'])
test_eq(len(live.hooks['after_tool']), 1)
test_eq([s.name for s in live.skills], [])
test_eq(live.loaded, False)
load(live, cfg=tmp)                                       # the files come back on the next read
test_eq([t.__name__ for t in live.tools], ['live_tool', 'word_count'])
live.drop_loaded()                                        # and a second round is not lossy
test_eq([t.__name__ for t in live.tools], ['live_tool'])
test_eq(Registry().drop_loaded().tools, [])               # never loaded: nothing to take back
```

Hooking an unknown event raises an error:

``` python
test_fail(lambda: reg.on('before_lunch', print), contains='unknown event')
```

A failing hook is recorded in `notes` and does not end the turn. Its
result is left out of what `fire` returns.

``` python
fired = []
reg.on('before_turn', lambda **kw: 1/0)
reg.on('before_turn', lambda **kw: fired.append(kw))
reg.fire('before_turn', prompt='hello'), fired, reg.notes[-1]
```

    (1,
     [{'prompt': 'hello'}],
     'before_turn hook failed: ZeroDivisionError: division by zero')

``` python
test_eq(fired, [{'prompt': 'hello'}])
test_eq(reg.fire('before_turn', prompt='again'), [None])
assert reg.notes[-1].startswith('before_turn hook failed'), reg.notes[-1]
```

An extension may replace the approval policy, the function that decides
whether a tool call goes ahead. The last one registered wins, and with
none registered `approve` is None.

``` python
@reg.approval
def approve_reads(tool, **kw): return not tool.startswith('write_')
reg.approve, reg.approve('view_file'), reg.approve('write_file')
```

    (<function __main__.approve_reads(tool, **kw)>, True, False)

``` python
test_eq(reg.approve.__name__, 'approve_reads')
test_eq(reg.approve('view_file'), True)
test_eq(reg.approve('write_file'), False)
test_eq(Registry().approve, None)                         # nothing registered approves everything
```

Extension folders inside a project load only with `project=True`.
Cloning a repository never runs its code.

``` python
test_eq([str(p) for p in ext_dirs(roots=['/proj'], cfg='/cfg')], ['/cfg/extensions'])
test_eq([str(p) for p in ext_dirs(roots=['/proj'], cfg='/cfg', project=True)][-1],
        '/proj/.leela/extensions')
```
